## 8. Next executed attack: dose-constrained pooling transition (changed physical interface)

The 124-query lower bound arose specifically because no allowed input could activate two gate locations simultaneously. Consider the **hypothetical stronger instrument** that accepts total dose `D` rather than `1/5`. Keep each gate's activation threshold at `tau=1/10`, and assume **at most one gate is present**, with its position unknown among the 124. Also supply a **trusted exact null-source reaction predictor for each proposed grouped action**. This predictor is an extra information contract, *not* acquired from the historical 932 scalar reactions.

At amplitude `a=101/1000` on every position of a set `A`, the extra shunt contributes to the actual four-node scalar port reaction

\[
\Delta R=50(a-\tau)^3=\frac1{20{,}000{,}000}=5\times10^{-8}
\]

if and only if the unique hidden gate lies in `A`; otherwise it contributes zero. This strictly exceeds `2epsilon=2e-8`, so a deterministic bounded-error raw-reaction observation can classify the group with no independent-noise premise. Physical feasibility requires `|A|a<=D`. Therefore each query can test at most `b=floor(D/a)` positions, and block scanning plus binary subdivision of a positive block has worst-case query count at most `ceil(124/b)+ceil(log_2 b)`.

`astra_activation_pooling.py` executed this on the exact-rational nonlinear four-node source at each newly stipulated dose budget, using Schur determinant evaluations (not mock sensor values), and reported correlated bounded-error scalar reactions:

| Hypothetical total-dose budget | Gates per group | Tests if no gate | Worst observed tests for selected hidden gates | Proved worst-case ceiling |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `0.2` (original) | 1 | 124 | 124 | 124 |
| `0.4` | 3 | 42 | 42 | 44 |
| `0.6` | 5 | 25 | 27 | 28 |
| `1.0` | 9 | 14 | 17 | 18 |

The improvement does **not** contradict the 124-query obstruction: the observation/actuation interface has changed, the component derivative bounds used in earlier all-actions certificates are not extended automatically to the larger domain, and the exact null-reaction predictor is an additional supplied capability. The experiment clarifies which new scientific instrument properties would make grouped identification possible. MATRIX-CONCAVE SCALAR AUDIT AND EXCITATION
Read the complete matrix-concavity proof, including its correction inside the
proof of Theorem2 and changed-interface section8. Antitonicity plus operator
convexity of inversion proves Z convex for jointly Loewner-concave Q. Direct
differentiation yields Zii=2pTQiQinverseQi p-pTQii p, nonnegative and bounded by
||e||²(2Li²/m³+Bi/m²). Integrating this curvature gives the stated forward-
difference brackets. The raw lower endpoint is (a0-bi)/hi-ci. The maximum with
-ci is valid ONLY with supplied monotone PSD actuation. Uniform SPD, concavity
and derivative caps alone do not supply monotonicity. Exact control Q(u)=2-u,
e=1,c=0 gives negative Gprime and a false zero lower endpoint if clipped.
At a positive interior candidate this can even produce a false zero regret
when the zero action is better. Retain the raw bound in the general theorem.
The n+1 reading audit composes with the same simplex dual, requires a live
resettable source and dose margin, and does not need a learned inverse matrix.

The cubic gate is C2, monotone and zero below threshold; total dose .2 permits
at most one coordinate strictly above .1. This verifies the finite-family
excitation/counting logic and conditional single-action regret argument when
the source-specific A_min,U0 and orthogonal-block construction hold. The base
matrices, all932 observations,768 derivatives and independent verifier archives
are missing, so their numeric and realization claims are not newly audited.
Do not turn the deterministic single-action regret bound into a randomized
expected-regret theorem. At amplitude .101, 50(.001)^3=5e-8>2e-8. With a trusted
exact group-null predictor, at most one gate and an actually permitted larger
dose D, block scanning and binary splitting give ceil(124/b)+ceil(log2 b),
b=floor(D/.101). At D=.4,.6,1 these ceilings are44,28,18, whereas null-source
counts are42,25,14. Earlier derivative caps do not extend to the new dose range.
This accepts the conditional algebra/counting, not safe physical higher doses.
